questions.q: In what year was Social Studies officially introduced into the Nigerian educational system on a pilot basis?
questions.explain: Social Studies was first introduced in Nigeria on a pilot basis in **1963** at the Comprehensive High School, Aiyetoro, located in present-day Ogun State.

questions.q: Which secondary school in Nigeria served as the experimental ground where Social Studies was first taught?
questions.explain: The teaching of Social Studies began at **Comprehensive High School, Aiyetoro**, serving as a model testing ground before the subject was gradually expanded to other Nigerian schools.

questions.q: Which of the following international organizations provided major funding and technical support for the introduction of Social Studies in Nigeria?
questions.explain: **The Ford Foundation**, along with the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), provided significant sponsorship and resources to facilitate the Aiyetoro Social Studies project.

questions.q: Before the introduction of the integrated Social Studies curriculum in Nigeria, which group of subjects was primarily taught to cover human interaction with society?
questions.explain: Prior to adopting an integrated approach, elements of human interaction, physical environment, and citizenship were taught separately as **History**, **Geography**, and **Civics**.

questions.q: What was the primary sociopolitical reason for introducing Social Studies in Nigeria shortly after independence?
options: To promote British colonial administrative culture
To foster national unity and integration
questions.explain: After independence, Nigeria recognized the need to bridge ethnic divisions. Social Studies was introduced as a tool to cultivate a sense of **shared identity, national unity, and integration** among its diverse population.

questions.q: Which prominent African conference held in 1968 played a highly significant role in shaping the adoption and curriculum development of Social Studies across the continent?
questions.explain: The **1968 Mombasa Conference** in Kenya brought African educators together and laid the regional groundwork for modern Social Studies curricula that emphasized indigenous needs and African environments.

questions.q: Under the Nigerian National Policy on Education (NPE), at what educational level is Social Studies mandated as a core and compulsory subject?
options: Basic Education level (Primary and Junior Secondary)
questions.explain: Social Studies is a core subject in the **Basic Education** curriculum (Primary 1 to JSS 3) to ensure foundational civic and moral development.
